Repair and extend the offline residential IPv6 campaign toolkit.
The multi-file Python workspace is in `/workspace/submission`.
Its generator, compressed capture classifier and device protocol adapters
must support the campaign interface specified in `/workspace/PROTOCOL.md`.
Implement revision-aware evidence reconciliation across prefix leases,
a causal service census, and an optimal quota-constrained follow-up plan.
Return the target manifest, rejected-record indices, snapshot reports,
request activity, and a checkable probe-script certificate.
All input addresses are documentation addresses; never contact targets.
Read `/workspace/SYSCALLS.md` for the exact child and checker-parent profiles.
Pinned dependencies are bundled; runtime and checks require no network.
Submit the entire `/workspace/submission` directory, with `campaign.py`
as its entry point. You may change, add or reorganize ordinary files.
The entry point receives one UTF-8 JSON object on stdin and writes one
UTF-8 JSON object on stdout. Other output belongs on stderr.
Run `python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/submission` for sanity checks.
The public examples cover only a small part of the stated domain.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
All work is complete and verified. Here's a summary of what I did:

## Repaired and extended `/workspace/submission`

**`campaign.py`** — entry point: reads ≤64 MiB JSON from stdin, enforces error precedence (metadata/JSON → exactly `{"error":"invalid"}`, capture transport/encoding/header/bounds → exactly `{"error":"capture"}`), pauses the cyclic collector during reconciliation, always flushes one JSON object to stdout and exits 0 (diagnostics on stderr).

**`common.py`** — bounded metadata validation (exact key sets, ID/time/prefix/forest rules, every count limit), strict envelope parsing (BOM, duplicate keys, nonfinite numbers, trailing data rejected), memoised compressed address spelling.

**`gen_targets.py`** — `plan()` expands canary + low IIDs per lease/subnet with the SHA-256 `seed\nlease\ncanonical-/64` canary IID ORed with 2⁶³, emitting the manifest in lease-lexical → subnet-numeric → canary-then-low order.

**`classify_responses.py`** — in-memory base64/zstd transport with complete-frame validation (window ≤128 MiB, dictionary-free, reserved bit, skippable/concatenated frames), bounded decompression, strict CSV logical-record framing, header check, 200 000-record/131 072-byte-field bounds, ordered `[capture, ordinal]` rejections; plus discovery role buckets, earliest causal witnesses and lease state priority (`inactive` > `alias` > `conflict` > `usable`).

**`ledger.py`** — typed 14-field record validation and hashable semantic contents (spelling-agnostic), with a revision ledger implementing highest-revision-wins, identical-content collapse, conflicts, tombstones and resurrection across increasing queries.

**`census.py`** — causal application census: eligibility (usable lease, clean role, witness ≤ event), max-attempt status decision, signature agreement, protocol errors, clean-role subsets, `internal_only` evidence comparison, snapshots and frozen request activity.

**`protocols.py`** — repaired ADB/sync wire parsers (exact framing, length/checksum/magic, command set, plist shape and duplicate-key semantics) and TCP/ADB/sync probe certificates.

**`planning.py`** — optimal quota-constrained plan: transversal-matroid greedy when both quota forests are provably slack, otherwise min-cost flow (own successive-shortest-path + Dinic primal-dual solver for small instances, bundled NetworkX simplex for large ones with an independent feasibility re-check and fallback).

**Validation**: both public fixtures pass byte-for-byte; ~50 spec-rule unit tests, transport/framing tests, metadata-envelope tests, a 3000-case fuzzer with a structural conformance checker, and >3000 random plan instances cross-checked against exhaustive enumeration and against all three solver routes. Max-scale sizing (200 000 records, 65 536 targets, 4096 requests, 8192 offers, 262 144 pairs) runs in seconds-to-~90 s with ~480 MiB RSS, and everything was re-verified under the scored seccomp filter.
